description:
Add Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) Type 2 coverage to the Write Primitives
benchmark. The MERGE category currently has 20 operations (overlap variants,
conditional update/insert, ETL aggregation, ROW_NUMBER deduplication, etc.)
but NONE exercise the canonical SCD Type 2 dimension-maintenance pattern:
close the current version of a changed row (set is_current = false and stamp
an end timestamp) and insert a new current version, keyed on a business key.

This is the single most common real-world MERGE workload in analytics ETL and
is a conspicuous gap. It is fully portable SQL - expressible as a standard
MERGE (or UPDATE + INSERT where MERGE is unavailable) on every platform the
benchmark targets (DuckDB, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse,
Databricks) - so it fits the benchmark's "broad platform compatibility,
non-transactional cleanup" design without compromise.

Motivation: a Databricks/Delta Lake post (SCD Type 2 via APPLY CHANGES INTO
vs ~200 lines of hand-written MERGE) highlighted the workload. The benchmark
should measure the portable MERGE form of this workload. The Databricks-native
declarative form (APPLY CHANGES INTO) is intentionally OUT OF SCOPE here - see
anti_patterns and deferred - and is evaluated narratively by the companion
blog TODO (blog-apply-changes-into-vs-standard-sql).

anti_patterns.dont: add APPLY CHANGES INTO (or any DLT / Lakeflow declarative pipeline syntax) as a benchmark operation
anti_patterns.instead: express SCD2 as portable MERGE/UPDATE+INSERT instead.
anti_patterns.why: it is not a standalone SQL statement and only runs inside a Databricks declarative pipeline, breaking the cross-platform + standalone-statement contract

anti_patterns.instead: derive the change set dynamically with percentage/range-bounded selects like the existing merge ops.
anti_patterns.why: the op must run at any scale factor

anti_patterns.instead: add dedicated scd2_ops_* staging tables instead.
anti_patterns.why: it lacks versioning columns and is shared by the existing 20 merge ops

deferrals.reason: Declarative APPLY CHANGES INTO requires a DLT/Lakeflow pipeline context (streaming source, pipeline run), not a SQL-warehouse session, so it cannot execute inside the current execute/validate/cleanup harness. Revisit if/when a pipeline-execution path exists. Tracked narratively by blog-apply-changes-into-vs-standard-sql.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Databricks APPLY CHANGES INTO needs a DLT/Lakeflow pipeline context unavailable in the current harness; tracked narratively by a blog post, not a TODO.
deferrals.summary: Databricks-native APPLY CHANGES INTO rewrite for the SCD2 op via sql_compat

deferrals.reason: Type 2 is the canonical history-retention workload and the one the source material highlights; add other types only if there is demand.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Type 1/Type 3 SCD variants explicitly gated on future demand beyond the canonical Type 2 workload; no evidence of demand.
